section: Educational Psychology · Ch6 — Intelligence & its Theories (Complete)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student excels at breaking down complex problems logically, comparing and evaluating different pieces of information, and scoring well on traditional academic tests requiring analysis and judgement. In Sternberg's Triarchic Theory, this ability is called:
explanation: Analytical (componential) intelligence involves logical analysis, comparison, and evaluation — the type of thinking traditional academic tests typically measure — completing Sternberg's Triarchic Theory alongside Practical (real-world problem-solving) and Creative (novel-solution) intelligence.
